method: Complete direct independent proof check; no new computation needed for these consequences. The finite-cascade dependency already has8392 exact checks and actual Opus5.5 review.

items.method_result: Read the symbol and nonzero-trace theorem statements, their explicit primary hypotheses and verification status. Both apply to the displayed smooth full-plane canonical profile.

For every proposed at-most-M-term approximant, one member of a fixed M+1 index set is absent. Orthogonality and integral |sin(j theta)|=4 give pi/4; Cauchy-Schwarz gives sqrt(pi). The infimum need not be attained.
Uniform trace convergence gives simultaneous convergence of any fixed finite set of Fourier coefficients; the positive limiting minimum excludes zero coefficients beyond one common radius.

The already checked finite-trace cascade supplies distinct n_k, nonzero A_k and strict epsilon_k for each finite k. The first M scaled coefficients diverge and the final one tends to |A_M|, so their minimum tends to |A_M|.

The conclusion is all sufficiently large r for every fixed M. It excludes a sequence with bounded count even if frequencies depend on r. No fixed-radius infinitude, monotonicity or uniform growth rate is inferred.

Each cutoff is supported away from zero; local finiteness follows from R_k going to infinity. The simultaneous j<=k cutoff inequalities imply the weighted geometric bound for k>=max(j,2K+2). Finitely many remaining higher terms have order at most s_(K+1). This proves all claimed derivative remainders, smoothness, parity and finite count per circle.
The general inverse lemma at b=p in (0,1) retains no negative multipole above p and gives U in S^p. The example has f_y(0)=0 and no transport equation is claimed. It is not a primary counterexample.
